variants.description: Multiple de novo missense variants (9 distinct variants across 12 patients)

clinical.citation: A Novel De Novo Gain-of-Function CACNA1D Variant in Neurodevelopmental Disease With Congenital Tremor, Seizures, and Hypotonia (PMID: 39246741)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: De novo variant with pronounced activity-enhancing gating changes (shift of channel activation and inactivation to more hyperpolarized potentials, impaired inactivation and deactivation) demonstrated by patch-clamp electrophysiology

clinical.citation: The human channel gating-modifying A749G CACNA1D (Cav1.3) variant induces a neurodevelopmental syndrome-like phenotype in mice (PMID: 37698939)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: De novo variant reported in patient with ASD and intellectual impairment; gating changes confirmed by heterologous expression and native LTCC recordings; mouse model (Cav1.3AG) reproduced human disease phenotype

clinical.citation: Pathogenicity of de novo CACNA1D Ca(2+) channel variants predicted from sequence co-variation (PMID: 38553610)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: Variant predicted pathogenic by evolutionary co-variation analysis; electrophysiological testing revealed significant gating changes associated with pathogenic risks

clinical.diagnostic_reason: De novo mutations identified in largest ASD whole-exome sequencing study (3,871 autism cases); CACNA1D implicated as gene involved in neuronal pacemaking and excitability-transcription coupling

clinical.citation: ASHG 2013 - Recurrently mutated genes contribute to the risk for developing sporadic autism spectrum disorder (ASHG 2013)

model_organism.citation: Ca(v) 1.3 (CACNA1D) L-type Ca(2+) channel dysfunction in CNS disorders (PMID: 26842699)
phenotypes: Loss of Cav 1.3 function does not result in neuropsychiatric or neurological disease symptoms
Acute selective pharmacological activation results in depressive-like behaviour

model_organism.citation: CACNA1D is a circadian gene and causes familial advanced sleep phase (PMID: 40460120)
phenotypes: Normal circadian period under constant darkness
Altered phase shifts in response to light in the subjective night at circadian time (CT) 16 and CT22

model_organism.citation: The SWI/SNF chromatin-remodeling subunit DPF2 regulates macrophage inflammation in intestinal injury via the CACNA1D-mediated MAPK pathway (PMID: 41223220)
phenotypes: Loss of Dpf2 in macrophages leads to loss of H3K27ac and H3K4me1 marks at Cacna1d enhancer
Attenuated mitogen-activated protein kinases signaling activity

model_organism.citation: CaBP1 and 2 enable sustained Ca(V)1.3 calcium currents and synaptic transmission in inner hair cells (PMID: 39718549)
phenotypes: Reduced availability of channels to trigger synaptic transmission
Strikingly reduced spontaneous and sound-evoked responses of spiral ganglion neurons in vivo
Responses strongly depend on stimulation rates

model_organism.citation: Retrocochlear function of the peripheral deafness gene Cacna1d (PMID: 22678062)
phenotypes: Dramatic volume reduction (43-47%) of major nuclei in superior olivary complex (SOC)
Reduced cell number in SOC (decline by 46-56%)
Abnormal formation of lateral superior olive at P4
Decreased amplitude in auditory nerve between 50 and 75 dB stimulation
Increased amplitudes in central auditory processing centers
No changes in Kv1.1, KCC2, or choline acetyltransferase expression

model_organism.citation: Zebrafish Larvae Carrying a Splice Variant Mutation in cacna1d: A New Model for Schizophrenia-Like Behaviours? (PMID: 33057948)
phenotypes: Heterozygous mutation resulted in 50% reduction of splice variants 201 and 202 (haploinsufficiency)
Homozygosity increased transcript levels of variant 201 above wild type (gain-of-function)
Altered locomotor activity under constant light
Altered startle response to dark flashes
Antipsychotics (risperidone and haloperidol) reversed hyperactivity to wild-type levels
Valproate decreased but did not reverse hyperactivity
No epileptiform-like discharges in larval brains

biological.citation: Calcium channelopathies and intellectual disability: a systematic review (PMID: 33985586)
biological.summary: CACNA1D identified as one of ten calcium channel genes associated with intellectual disability and global developmental delay. Both gain-of-function and loss-of-function variants implicated, with gain-of-function variants associated with more severe phenotypes. Mechanisms include altered channel kinetics and dominant-negative effects.

biological.citation: CACNA1D-Related Channelopathies: From Hypertension to Autism (PMID: 36592224)
biological.summary: CACNA1D encodes the pore-forming α1 subunit of Cav1.3 L-type calcium channels. De novo missense variants cause gain-of-function through activity-enhancing gating changes, leading to increased Ca2+ influx. Associated with neurodevelopmental disorders, hypertension, and congenital hypoglycemia. Dihydropyridine LTCC inhibitors proposed as therapeutic option.

biological.citation: The human channel gating-modifying A749G CACNA1D (Cav1.3) variant induces a neurodevelopmental syndrome-like phenotype in mice (PMID: 37698939)
biological.summary: In heterozygous Cav1.3AG mice carrying the A749G variant, native LTCC currents in adrenal chromaffin cells showed predicted gating changes. The mutation induced aberrant excitability in dopamine neurons and medium spiny neurons. Phenotype reproduced developmental delay, social deficit, and hyperactivity without major neuroanatomical changes.

biological.citation: De novo CACNA1D Ca(2+) channelopathies: clinical phenotypes and molecular mechanism (PMID: 32583268)
biological.summary: CACNA1D variants identified somatically in aldosterone-producing adenomas and germline in neurodevelopmental disorder patients. In vitro heterologous expression studies revealed gating changes indicating enhanced Ca2+ influx as the disease mechanism. Proposes using somatic mutations in adenomas to predict pathogenicity of novel germline variants.

biological.citation: Update on the Genetics of Primary Aldosteronism and Aldosterone-Producing Adenomas (PMID: 35841527)
biological.summary: CACNA1D identified as one of five major genes (KCNJ5, CACNA1D, ATP1A1, ATP2B3, CTNNB1) harboring variants in aldosterone-producing adenomas. Pathogenic variants alter ion transportation and cell membrane depolarization, leading to aldosterone overproduction. CACNA1D also found mutated in germline state causing familial hyperaldosteronism.

CACNA1D identified as one of six genes (KCNJ5, ATP1A1, ATP2B3, CACNA1D, CACNA1H, CLCN2) with genetic defects in aldosterone-producing tumors and hyperplasias. These genes modify intracellular calcium signaling, distinguishing them from cAMP-pathway genes involved in cortisol-producing tumors.

CACNA1D mutations identified as major drivers in aldosterone-producing adenomas through exome sequencing. Intracellular calcium signaling highlighted as central to APA pathophysiology, with CACNA1D mutations serving as potential basis for targeted medical treatments.

biological.citation: ASHG 2017 - African ancestry genome- and transcriptome-wide association study of blood pressure detects nine novel loci in a large cohort from the Million Veteran Program
biological.summary: CACNA1D identified as most significant locus for diastolic blood pressure in African Americans (p-value = 1.26x10^-12). Predicted reduced expression of TMEM110 near the CACNA1D GWAS signal in nucleus accumbens-basal ganglia associated with systolic blood pressure, suggesting TMEM110 as relevant gene in that region.
biological.sample_size: ~59,900 African Americans from Million Veteran Program

biological.citation: ASHG 2018 - GWAS of resistant hypertension in over 70,000 participants from the Million Veteran Program identifies genes with altered expression in the adrenal gland
biological.summary: CACNA1D identified in genome-wide significant association with resistant hypertension in African Americans (two SNPs near CACNA1D). CACNA1D is targeted by calcium channel blockers commonly used in African ancestry patients, suggesting clinical relevance for treatment.
biological.sample_size: 16,830 resistant hypertension cases, 53,376 controlled hypertension controls
biological.significance: Genome-wide significant in African Americans only

biological.citation: ASHG 2015 - Identification of rare disruptive variants in voltage-gated channel genes (CACNA1C, CACNA1D, CACNA1S, CACNA1I) in Japanese samples of schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorder using Ion Torrent PGM platform
biological.summary: Mutation screening of CACNA1D in Japanese schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorder samples identified 1 nonsense variant (p.C1471*), 1 in-frame deletion (p.E1675del), and multiple damaging missense variants. Findings suggest dysregulation of cellular calcium homeostasis via L-type voltage-gated calcium channels in psychiatric disorder pathogenesis.
biological.sample_size: 370 schizophrenia patients, 192 autism spectrum disorder patients
